forecaster_note: A bit of south swell left – chest high or so at the exposures, clean at the south-facing breaks with N winds. Not a standout day, but there should be fun sized waves at the south exposures; elsewhere lumpier and junkier as short-period NE swell fills in. — Tim Williams, Surfline. Water temp is estimated (no live station feed this run).

wind.summary: NNW 7–10 km/h and offshore at dawn, cross-shore by 9am, NE 16 km/h onshore by 3pm.

shark.summary: 2 tagged white shark detections at Palm Beach last night (6:15pm and 5:49pm), about 20 km north of Dee Why. No detections at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the past 24h. Feed live — newest NSW detection 6 min ago.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small and south-leaning. 102 kJ sits well under your 450 floor – a finesse morning, not a power day. Long Reef and Curl Curl hold offshore NNW through midday; Dee Why turns cross-shore by 9am.

swells.label: S groundswell – wraps soft at Dee Why
Small ENE mid-period – best angle here

dee-why.window: Dawn to 9am while it is still offshore. NE fills in by 3pm and ends it.
alerts: S 175° swell wraps badly here – expect it softer than the numbers read.

tip.label: Frontside
tip.text: The Point right is your frontside wall, but at 2–3ft off 175° it is a soft shoulder. Stay high, keep speed, do not hunt the turn.

long-reef.window: 9am–12pm. Offshore NNW the whole window – pick of the four.

tip.label: Frontside
tip.text: The right off the point is frontside for you and has the best shape of the morning. This is where the 3–4ft actually stands up.

curl-curl.window: 9am–12pm on the offshore; NE cross-shore from 3pm.

tip.label: Backside
tip.text: Banks favour the lefts here – backside for you, so commit early off the top rather than stalling for the section.

manly.window: Cross-shore from dawn – only worth it for a quick one.

tip.label: Mixed
tip.text: North Steyne peaks both ways. Take the rights to stay frontside; the lefts are short and closing out.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Fading – 74 kJ and mostly thigh-high, though consistency spikes to 98%. Offshore W/SW until about 10am, then SE onshore shuts it down by noon.

dee-why.window: Early only – SE onshore from noon.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 9am, best of a quiet day.

curl-curl.window: Dawn window before the SE swings on.

manly.window: Offshore till midday here – holds on longest of the four.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the day – 138 kJ, WNW offshore right through the morning, Long Reef 3–5ft and Curl Curl to 5ft. Sunday collapses to knee-high. Plan Saturday AM.

dee-why.window: Sat morning – WNW offshore till midday. Sunday is knee-high, skip it.

long-reef.window: Sat 6am–12pm is the weekend's best window, chest to head.

curl-curl.window: Sat morning, offshore all the way to midday.

manly.window: Smallest of the four both days – Sat AM or not at all.
